When I joined this gym last year, I wasn’t just looking for a workout plan; I was looking for a trainer who could make the gym feel like a place where I belonged. That’s when I met Akshay.

From day one, it wasn’t just his knowledge of fitness that stood out, but his ability to meet me as a person first. As a queer trans man, that mattered deeply. He asked my pronouns, listened to my concerns, and adjusted so I felt respected.

Akshay knows his stuff, from form corrections to intelligent programming, but what makes him invaluable is his patience and consistency. He’ll call you out if you skip, but never to shame you. His point is always clear: showing up matters, but persistence is what leads to growth. That mindset has kept me going when I might’ve quit. He also understands the impact training has on mental health, and he treats progress as more than just physical results.

In a year, I’ve grown stronger not only in what I lift, but in my posture, confidence, and how I carry myself. I didn’t quit this time, and that’s because Akshay gave me the structure and support to keep showing up.

The gym itself has been just as important in making this possible. I feel safe in the space; there’s camaraderie, respect, and nobody makes me feel like I don’t belong. Even if people don’t fully understand all my concerns, they hold space and are supportive. The facilities are excellent too, with everything a beginner or advanced gym-goer might need: a wide variety of machines, crossfit setups, cardio, and strength equipment. I didn’t find this kind of support at other gyms I tried in Mulund, and that’s what makes this one stand out.
